compareDisposition.rationale: The curator examined Curse ends in siege, scattering, and return to Egypt beside The land is said to vomit out its inhabitants; Scattering is threatened and covenant is remembered; The wilderness generation is refused entry; Scattering and seeking are held together. Those passages share its Eden-and-exile evidence group or canonical movement, but none supplies a distinct two-source relationship stronger than the accepted comparisons already carrying this topic.

payload.posture: Read “Curse ends in siege, scattering, and return to Egypt” as its own Scripture scene before carrying its imagery into another heavenly gathering.
payload.tension: the passage shows defilement, covenant breach, threatened removal, and historical loss of land, while historical exile remains a concrete event even when its patterns echo earlier expulsion.
